title: Cruising with hands on the furniture is a CDC line at about 1 year
summary: Most babies walk while holding on to furniture by about 1 year, the US CDC says.
body: Hands stay planted on a sofa, a table, or another piece of furniture while the feet step. The CDC 1-year page prints that pattern as walks, holding on to furniture. It is its own movement line, beside the haul up to standing, among things most babies do by one year. Empty hands are a different age on a later page. This cruise is the US figure. Another country's list can disagree.

sources.title: Milestones by 1 Year
sources.author: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention
sources.note: Movement line: Walks, holding on to furniture.
